theme: Original mythical keeper of patterned-fen memory: three thick peat-rib fingers hover around a small teardrop tree-island head, with two clean dark pool gaps between them. It reads a past season from each layer and can fold one forgotten path into another. The name refers to flark pools, not an existing sacred spirit. Its spectral recollections and path-folding are an original Ghost/Fairy enchantment.
evolution_design: Single-stage mythical: three broad offset peat-rib fingers form a cupped hand around the teardrop head; two large pool gaps stay open, one short root tassel hangs below. Keep three ribs only for native readability.

silhouettes.front: Small cupped three-rib peat hand with teardrop island head and two pool gaps.
silhouettes.back: Large back of upper peat ribs and tree-island nape, lower tassel cropped.

habitat: A proposed Big Bog-inspired patterned-fen side area, geographically a northwest optional spur from the Bemidji/Border Pines area rather than an invented claim that Waskish is already on MN_R17.

sources.evidence: Patterned peatlands include raised bogs, transverse peat ribs, pools and water tracks.
sources.fantasy_extension: Peat patterns become visible creature anatomy and fictional memory channels.

sources.publisher: Minnesota DNR Big Bog State Recreation Area
sources.evidence: Big Bog near Waskish includes extensive patterned peatland and a boardwalk viewpoint.
sources.fantasy_extension: The fictional memory encounter is viewed from an authored boardwalk-inspired safe path; no real protected land is altered.

location: Proposed Memory Flark, a fictional optional boardwalk vista in a future Big Bog-inspired side area; no existing authored map/encounter is asserted.
mythical_narrative: A short optional survey records three rib/pool patterns at different times. Flarkindle appears only when the player restores the pattern on a small map, representing peatland time and memory. Its lore is wholly original and does not reinterpret an Indigenous sacred being.
